notes.title: The Story Behind Dying Breed + We have a release date!
notes.content:
[p]Hello everyone,[/p][p]
Ignacio Trelles here, creator of Dying Breed. With release approaching, I wanted to take a step back and share the long road that led us here, from childhood inspirations, through countless setbacks, to finally seeing this project come alive. Also the game will be available on the 7th of October! How cool is that?

[/p][h2]Childhood Inspirations[/h2][p]
I grew up in Uruguay, where getting original PC games was not easy, but somehow we were lucky enough to have them. My first titles were Tiberian Dawn, Red Alert, Total Annihilation, and Age of Empires, all played straight from their original boxes.
Later came Heroes of Might and Magic III, RollerCoaster Tycoon, Civilization, Diablo, Warcraft, Empire Earth, Baldur’s Gate, and more. Most of the games I loved shared one thing in common: the 2.5D isometric perspective. That visual style shaped my taste and still defines how I approach game design today.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43693320/931d611ae4c25428c155bdbaad88049d3b15b321.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43693320/a7610af87b13dc3d1cbbfe465b720a588d1b465e.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]The Spark to Create[/b][/h2][p]The idea of starting a business in games appeared in 2018. By mid-2019, I had decided to create one from scratch.[/p][p]I began researching game development and rediscovered [i]Xenonauts[/i], a reimagining of the classic [i]UFO: Enemy Unknown[/i], the very first PC game I ever played, back when my cousin and I were 7 years old at a neighbor’s house. That gave me the idea: what if I could remake or reimagine something old, like cinema does with movie remakes ([i]Invasion of the Body Snatchers[/i], for example)?[/p][p]I made a list of three potential inspirations: [i]GTA2[/i], [i]Heroes of Might and Magic III[/i], and [i]Command & Conquer[/i]. My instinct was to avoid [i]C&C[/i], thinking it would be the hardest to achieve. But my investor thought the opposite: [i]if others did it, why can’t we?[/i] And so, we had a plan.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43693320/a9127efe18b90776c35c54f33faf77dc7cbc8a75.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]A Name, a Story, a Vision[/b][/h2][p]The name [i]Dying Breed[/i] had been with me since the mid-2000s, originally the name of a clan in [i]Lineage 2[/i], back in the cybercafé era. Within two days, I wrote the story, mixing Lovecraftian tones with 80s B-movie sci-fi vibes (with inspirations from Commandos, Command & Conquer and Heroes 3).[/p][p]From the start, I wanted [i]Dying Breed[/i] to focus on drama and single-player storytelling, unlike many RTS games at the time that were multiplayer-focused. We even drafted a movie and prepared a music album to go alongside the project.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43693320/ae8c0555264e471528f1a639ef2f7e1802f64819.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43693320/ed5a601531a68b0a43c05dd9a1768521715f6df3.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]Early Struggles[/b][/h2][p]In late 2019, I broke my Achilles tendon and spent three months at home in a cast. I played [i]0 A.D.[/i] obsessively, becoming one of the best players, meeting its devs, and befriending many Linux users in Europe. That “do it yourself” spirit became part of me.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43693320/c13fdb656174f03cc619eec338a0ce3f846a9bf1.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Our first team struggled. The coder produced nothing after three months, the first artist left due to personal issues, and we lost a year (but we learned a lot about business and team management). The second team showed promise, but again, we lost people to bigger companies. Finally, in the third attempt, a [i]0 A.D.[/i] engineer joined, along with a dedicated new artist, and that’s when things really started to move.[/p][p]
[/p][h2][b]Demos, Pitches & Publishing Drama[/b][/h2][p]We launched our first demo on October 11, 2021. The next day, we had a publishing offer, but internal disagreements killed the deal. Frustrated, I staged what I call a “coup d’état” in the company and took over decision-making.[/p][p]By late 2022, we pitched to 12 publishers. Six were interested, but one by one, they disappeared or delayed. Tired of waiting, I sent the second demo to Splattercat. He uploaded a video almost instantly, and [i]Dying Breed[/i] gained its first real wave of fans.[/p][p]That’s when I set up the Steam page. Within three months, MicroProse reached out. They had been part of my childhood, with [i]Civilization[/i] and [i]RollerCoaster Tycoon[/i] shaping my gaming life. When they said they wanted to publish [i]Dying Breed[/i], I didn’t hesitate.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Building the Game[/b][/h2][p]From there, the team grew. We brought in new engineers, artists, and even won a state fund in Uruguay that allowed us to record FMV cutscenes with live actors, just like the old-school RTS classics.[/p][p]We produced two OSTs, each faction having its own music style. Friends helped compose 19 songs, and even sold some to other games later on.[/p][p]Map design became another passion. I personally designed many maps, but we now have four different designers whose styles you’ll notice in-game. We also integrated 3D FMV sequences, hired riggers and modelers, and kept building nonstop.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43693320/6502e24e626ebf6440ea5748fc18021ad9b653e5.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43693320/36fc620c58ea848fcd2654cc69d4eb8a879fda5f.png"][/img][/p][h2][b]The Long Road to Launch[/b][/h2][p]Making [i]Dying Breed[/i] was never easy. We lost people, had setbacks with Unity, faced broken builds, and had to cut down the number of missions for launch. But we never stopped.[/p][p]Over the years, I’ve helped over 20 other games get publishing deals, composed music and sounds for others, and met countless indie devs I admire. This journey has been life-changing, full of ups, downs, and lessons.[/p][p]Our motto has always been: [b]NEVER SURRENDER[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43693320/26dd9cb809e5679f62f850d42dc63267a8a71231.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43693320/2322838b93a94186dd3983832601f0ea136f1bb1.jpg"][/img][/p][h2][b]Closing Thoughts[/b][/h2][p][i]Dying Breed[/i] is my love letter to the first generation of base-building RTS games. It’s also the result of years of persistence, friendships, failures, and victories.[/p][p]I can’t wait for you to experience the world we’ve built, its story, its music, its FMVs, and its brutal, strategic battles.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43693320/2df03533c01c17acf271089e6b6c5ab5c2d9ee84.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43693320/e848b62887c9a6aebbcd66806e433654e654a11a.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p]P.S. I almost forgot, [url="https://playdyingbreed.com/new/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Manual_DB_EN_Z.pdf"][u]we have a manual![/u][/url] Have a nice read!


[/p]

notes.title: Retro-RTS Dying Breed comes complete with campy FMV cutscenes
notes.content: In the golden age of the RTS we thought that FMV cutscenes were really cool and fun. Then, later on, we decided they were very bad and made us cringe. Now we have come full circle and realize that they are good, actually... Read more.

notes.title: MicroProse Announced as Publisher for Dying Breed!
notes.content:
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/37756818/224847f3a14e32639f190cbcf3cb924b4bdb7d8f.jpg[/img]

Dying Breed Fans, today we announce MicroProse is our publisher! It’s a perfect match for an old-school golden-age RTS!

Have you seen the trailer on the Steam page?

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2088550/Dying_Breed/

[b]About Dying Breed[/b]
Are you ready to enter a time machine that will bring you straight back to when the RTS genre was born?

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/37756818/077515abccddb4733d90ddda9336573f70226d08.gif[/img]

Set in a twisted WW2 reality, this thrilling title blends fast-paced action with strategic decision-making, offering a unique gameplay experience. In Dying Breed, you will fight evil arch-enemies, zombies, and encounter retro-futuristic technologies. The game features fast-paced action, classic RTS mechanics, and encourages players to be both cunning and sneaky when necessary.

[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/37756818/bb84aa87c11461e331f839804297bb91f863597a.gif[/img]

Get ready for a world filled with shiny energy minerals, underground monsters, and warring factions, complemented by live-action FMVs and a '90s metal soundtrack. It's a love letter to classic RTSs, a tribute to science fiction cult movies, and an homage to game OSTs.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2088550/Dying_Breed/

notes.title: Hello Steam!
notes.content:
Hello Steam!

 We are Sarnayer Studio, a small indie company located in Uruguay!
Mid 2018 we had the idea of creating a first generation RTS game inspired
in the ones we used to play when we where young. 
In March 2019 we start investigating how to achive it; art, code, sound and music!
in 2020 we had our first playable build with all the basic and 
in October 2021 we published our first demo on www.playdyingbreed.com website.
in October 2022 we published our second demo for sending it to publishers and
this year we made it public on out itch.io page.
We divided the game production in 3 parts, currently 2 are already done.
Third part should consist in base building and UI/UX art and code.
We need all the support to keep on working on what we love: Making games!
